narrative:
The model predicts you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, the system flags it as enough of a risk that you are required to take remedial courses to strengthen your preparation.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. First, you have had no past class failures, which is exactly average for students who passed. This record actually pulls the prediction strongly toward passing. Second, you are not receiving extra educational support at school. Because almost all students who succeed do not need this support either, the absence of it slightly increases the model’s concern about your readiness. Third, you have a clear desire to pursue higher education, something every successful student in the data also expressed. This ambition works in your favor and helps push the prediction back toward passing.

Even though your clean failure record and educational goals are working to protect you, the lack of school support tips the balance just enough for the model to recommend extra help. 

To improve, consider reaching out for structured academic support now, even if you have managed without it before. Reducing your 10 absences (more than double the average of students who passed) would also remove a hidden risk. Taking these steps can turn a borderline prediction into a confident pass.
